ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A large square is divided into a small square surrounded by four congruent rectangles as shown. The perimeter of each of the congruent rectangles is 14. What is the area of the large square?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a large square, and the interior is divided in a pinwheel shape: in the middle is a small square, and around it are respectively a horizontal rectangle above, a vertical rectangle on the right side, a horizontal rectangle below, and a vertical rectangle on the left side; these four rectangles have the same shape, only some have been rotated in direction. Then reason: Let the side lengths of each congruent rectangle be a and b. According to the pinwheel-shaped arrangement in the figure, one side of the large square is made up of one long side of an adjacent rectangle and another short side, so the side length of the large square is a+b. The perimeter of each rectangle is 14, therefore 2(a+b)=14, obtaining a+b=7. So the side length of the large square is 7, and the area is 7^2=49.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a pinwheel-like division of a large square: the top and bottom pieces are horizontal rectangles, the left and right pieces are congruent rotated rectangles, and the center is a small square. Let each congruent rectangle have side lengths a and b. From the diagram, one side of the large square is made from one long side and one short side of two adjacent rectangles, so the large square side length is a+b. From the text, each rectangle has perimeter 14, so 2(a+b)=14 and a+b=7. Therefore the large square has side 7 and area 7^2=49.

Each of the four sides of the large square is formed by two exposed rectangle sides: one short side and one long side from congruent rectangles.
